entities.summary: Audie Leon Murphy was an American soldier, actor, and songwriter. He was widely celebrated as the most decorated American combat soldier of World War II, and has been described as the most highly decorated enlisted soldier in U.S. history. He received every military combat award for valor available from the United States Army, as well as French and Belgian awards for heroism. Murphy received the Medal of Honor for valor that he demonstrated at age 19 for single-handedly holding off a company of German soldiers for an hour at the Colmar Pocket in France in January 1945, before leading a successful counterattack while wounded.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Audie Murphy's heroism at the Colmar Pocket in January 1945 led to a successful counterattack despite being wounded, contributing significantly to the Allied victory in World War II. His numerous awards and decorations have made him an iconic figure in American history.
